rv.q: Whether you prefer the foghorn drawl of Ms. Turner or the more soothing tones of Dr. Drew, of “Celebrity Rehab” fame, is essentially just a matter of taste.
Too bad the writing isn’t sufficiently nuanced to make her calvary more affecting.
Now if we could only get Turner back onstage in a role worthy of her.
Turner does her best to bring warmth and intelligence to the brass-knuckled nun, but this troubled saint remains a flimsy character in a hollow play.
But if you grew up watching Bugs Bunny and "The Wizard of Oz" instead of Nickelodeon and "High School Musical," then you'll likely find "Wonderland" to be too namby-pamby for words.
Turner brings her patented husky swagger to the main role, but to little effect; she’s mother superior to a thin weepie that’s quite inferior.
It's shameful that High never manages to dig any deeper in that moment or any moment.
Alas, for the most part, High gave me a crisis of my own.
Nevertheless, the play comes off as a dull three-character mystery that pales in comparison with more compelling thrillers such as "Equus" and "Agnes of God."

cn.t: Turner commands attention in this melodramatic addiction tale, but critics find Lombardo's script trashy and manipulative, with clichéd dialogue undermining the star's fierce performance.

sg.ra: The Booth is one of Broadway's smallest houses at 766 seats, so center orchestra rows C-H give close-up detail of plays and intimate dramas without paying the very-front premium. Row AA front offers max legroom (Headout) but stage is high; step back a few rows for better sightline onto the stage floor.

sg.vl: Workable angle, not the sweet spot
sg.ra: Booth is narrow so side orchestra remains viable, but a 2018 BWW forum post specifically flagged 'angle from the front side seats' as a concern. Closer rows (BB, A) on the side get awkward angles onto the high stage. Mid-house aisle seats recover the view while adding legroom.
sg.rr: A-P (17 rows, odd 1-15 left, even 2-16 right)

sg.ra: In a 252-seat mezzanine with only 8 rows, even the back row is close. SeatPlan and Headout both call Center Mezz A-B some of the best seats in the house, and G-H are cited as strong value. With the Booth's intimate scale, the mezzanine never feels distant — this is the value pick.

sg.vl: Small house saves the side angle
sg.ra: SeatPlan explicitly notes side-mezz views are 'slightly more angled but still viable' because the Booth is narrow. Decent budget alternative, but the center mezz is a better value at similar price tier so this is solid-not-sweet.
